name: Tool start
description: Adapter plate that bolts to the robot flange and carries the connection to the tool end. Flange geometry comes from flanges.json; everything here is a user setting or a rule derived from it.

screws.count: all threaded holes of the selected flange (no count option)
screws.size: taken from the flange thread (M5 for the KR 4 R600)

options.label: Plate
options.note: Best for printing from the base without supports. The dowel keeps the rotation aligned, but there is no centering spigot, so concentric alignment is weaker.

thickness.description: General thickness (t) of everything the tool start makes: plate, spigot wall and collar wall.
thickness.notRecommended: below 1.5 (the minimum of 1 is allowed but flagged)

tolerances.description: Each value is an offset applied to each side of a surface (a hole grows by 2x the value in diameter, a peg shrinks by 2x the value in diameter).

dowelHole.note: Press-fit hole for a metal dowel, so the range is small.

dowelPin.note: Printed dowel only. Proposed values, not yet confirmed.

dowel.description: Alignment feature that fixes the plate's rotation, matching the locating pin hole in the flange.

options.label: Hole for a metal dowel pin
options.diameter: flange pin diameter + 2 x dowel hole tolerance

options.label: Printed pin (not recommended)
options.diameter: flange pin diameter - 2 x printed dowel tolerance
options.length: min(shared depth, flange pin depth) - printed dowel tolerance
options.warning: Not recommended: printed pins are weaker and less accurate than a metal dowel because of printing tolerance and strength limits.

plate.outerDiameter: max(flange spigot diameter or outer diameter, collar outer diameter, 2 x (pitch circle radius + head cylinder diameter / 2 + plate edge margin)). Always sized for the screw head. With away-facing chamfers the margin grows by 2 x chamfer size.
plate.centreHole: plate: flange centre hole diameter, left empty. plate-spigot and plate-spigot-collar: spigot bore.

spigot.outerDiameter: flange centre hole diameter - 2 x spigot tolerance
spigot.example: KR 4 R600, t = 1.5, tolerance 0.3: outer 19.4, bore 16.4, length 5.2

collar.innerDiameter: flange spigot diameter + 2 x collar tolerance

screwHole.diameter: screw nominal diameter + 2 x screw hole tolerance

geometryRules.screwArrangement: The head cylinder of each screw must not overlap its neighbours. On the KR 4 R600 the closest screw centres are 12.05 apart, so cylinders up to 10 never overlap.
geometryRules.featureDepth: Shared depth for the spigot and the collar: min(flange centre hole depth, flange spigot height) minus the larger of the spigot and collar tolerances. KR 4 R600: min(6, 5.5) = 5.5, minus 0.3 at the defaults = 5.2. Taking the larger tolerance guarantees neither feature bottoms out. In Plate mode (no spigot) a printed pin uses min(flange spigot height, centre hole depth) - spigot tolerance, capped by the flange pin depth minus the spigot tolerance.

dowelHole.diameter: flange pin diameter + 2 x dowel hole tolerance

screwClearance.description: Negative cylinder cut for the screw head (assumes socket head cap screws, ISO 4762). Opens on the face away from the robot.
screwClearance.headSource: ISO 4762, plain head: dk max (head diameter) and k max (head height = nominal diameter). M18 is not in ISO 4762; its values are from DIN 912. M1 and M1.2 have no socket head cap screw standard, so they are not listed.

length.description: How deep the cylinder cuts into the plate from the face the screws are inserted from.
length.examples: head height 5: t = 3 gives 2, t = 6 gives 5, t = 8 gives 5

countersink.rule: Disabled if less than 1 mm of material would remain under the countersink.
countersink.message: Less than 1 mm of material would remain under the countersink. Increase the thickness.

counterbore.rule: Never disabled. Yellow warning when the head would stand proud of the plate.
counterbore.message: {proud} mm of the socket head would stand proud due to your selected thickness.

chamfer.description: Optional 45 degree chamfers on convex edges of planar faces, to make printing easier and screws easier to start.

robotFacing.applies: convex edges of faces that face the robot: plate bottom outer edge, spigot and collar end edges, screw and dowel hole edges on the robot side, printed pin tip

awayFacing.applies: convex edges of faces that face away from the robot: plate top outer edge, centre hole top edge, screw and dowel hole entry edges, counterbore rim and counterbore floor hole edge. Countersinks are not chamfered because the cone already is a lead-in.

chamfer.notChamfered: inside corners (where walls meet the plate) so mating fits are not affected
chamfer.warning: Chamfers are disabled below 1.5 mm thickness because both sides of a wall would meet.

plateEdgeMargin.description: Extra material beyond the screw head cylinder at the plate edge. The plate is always sized for an Allen screw head, with or without a seat.

wallKeys.description: Some flanges have pockets cut into a wall (wallPockets in flanges.json). When on, the tool start gets one key per pocket so it locks into them.
wallKeys.spigotKeys: Pockets in the flange centre hole wall: a key sticks out of the spigot wall. Plate + Spigot and Plate + Spigot + Collar.
wallKeys.collarKeys: Pockets in the flange raised spigot wall: a key sticks inward from the collar wall. Plate + Spigot + Collar only.
wallKeys.keyDiameter: pocket diameter - 2 x tolerance of the wall that touches it (spigot tolerance for spigot keys, collar tolerance for collar keys)
wallKeys.keyLength: min(shared depth, pocket depth - that tolerance), so the key ends on the same plane as the spigot or collar
wallKeys.direction: Angles are measured from the pin hole, seen from the tool side. 'clockwise' or 'counterclockwise' is set per flange in flanges.json.

viewMesh.note: Mesh of the robot side in the 3D view (not the export). Smaller = smoother, slower.
